## Summary

Main Street side of the Steam follow-to-unlock feature (core CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC, F5). Adds a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action to the tutorial's final completion step (T26):

- `UnifiedTutorialStepDef.showSteamFollowCta` opt-in flag (T26 set).
- `MainStreetTutorialHints` renders the CTA in the completion tooltip: it opens the Steam store/community page through the launcher bridge (`window.tce.steamFollow`) when present, falls back to the web store page in a plain browser, and re-checks the follow (auto-detection, or the manual self-attest claim when the Steamworks binding has no `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`).
- The CTA is additive — the existing "Let's play!" button still finishes the tutorial; following is never required (graceful degradation).
- Copy added to `tutorial-en.csv` (`tutorial.steamFollow.*`), keeping the CSV integrity contract green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The tutorial's final step shows the Steam follow CTA (SLL-independent: it lives in the existing completion tooltip).
- [ ] Launcher mode opens the Steam page via the bridge; browser mode opens the web store page with copy explaining no reward is granted there.
- [ ] The follow is re-checked after the page opens; an unlock is surfaced as a status message.
- [ ] The CTA never blocks finishing the tutorial; a missing bridge or a rejected bridge call degrades to a status message.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the flag wiring, the CSV keys, and the bridge/browser branching.
- [ ] `npm test` (unit) and `npm run build` pass in this repo.

## Description

Create unit tests that verify per-seat competitive scoring — each seat receives challenge bonus points only for challenges it personally completed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `updateCompetitiveScores` awards `challengeBonusPoints` only for challenges where the seat's ID matches the completing seat.
2. A seat that has not completed any challenges receives no challenge bonus.
3. A seat that completed N challenges receives N × challengeBonusPoints.
4. Single-player scoring remains unchanged (global challengesCompleted.length × challengeBonusPoints).
5. Per-seat scoring is consistent with the attribution records created by the challenge evaluation path.

## Implementation

- Tests in `tests/main-street/challenge-scoring-per-seat.test.ts`
- Tests verify the `updateCompetitiveScores` function directly with attributed state.

- `tests/main-street/challenge-scoring-per-seat.test.ts` — New test file
- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — updateCompetitiveScores
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — PlayerRecord.score

## Summary

## Verification approach

- Add `tests/main-street/PackSourceRegistry.test.ts` covering source ordering, additive registration, unknown pack refs and total degradation.

# Pack-source registry and bundled source

**Parent:** MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD (Make card packs available in the browser distribution)

## Summary

Introduce a game-side pack-source registry so Main Street resolves card-pack content from an ordered set of interchangeable sources, and implement the first non-Electron source: a build-time bundled source that carries the production residential pack.

## Goal (user story)

> As a developer, I want the packs bundled into the web build automatically, so shipping a pack needs no manual content-directory install step.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` defining a `PackSource` (resolve the manifest text and one pack's CSV/asset content by pack ref) plus an ordered `PackSourceRegistry` consulted in source order.
- Implement the bundled source with Vite `import.meta.glob` (`?raw` for `manifest.json` and `cards.csv`, `?url` for assets) so the production pack is baked into the bundle. If the implementer instead chooses the `virtual:card-pack-registry` Vite-plugin shape (mirroring `virtual:game-registry`), record that decision in this item.
- Wire the registry into `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` through the existing injectable `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` transport seams, so the core loader is unchanged.
- Keep the registry total: an unknown pack ref, a missing bundled file, or an empty registry degrades to base content and never throws.
- Add the `?raw` / `?url` module declarations to `env.d.ts` if required.

## Deliverables

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` (registry + bundled source) and wiring in `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
- Unit tests for source ordering, additive registration and total degradation
- Module doc comments describing how to add a new source

## Dependencies

- None. `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (remote hosting) depends on this item and is out of scope here.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts`
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
- `tests/main-street/PackSourceRegistry.test.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

- The pack-source abstraction resolves Main Street card-pack content from at least one non-Electron source (the bundled source) and is structured so a same-origin or remote source can be added **additively** without changing the core loader or the listing (the remote source itself is out of scope — `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC`).
- The bundled source supplies manifest and `cards.csv` text to the existing `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` loader seams, with no change to the core loader (`core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts`).
- The web build (`npm run build` → `dist/`) embeds the production residential pack (manifest, `cards.csv` and assets) with **no manual `<contentDir>/packs/` copy step**; a build-artefact assertion proves the pack is present in the emitted `dist/`.
- Pack CSV and asset URLs resolve in the browser with **no `tce-packs://` request**; either the bundled source supplies same-origin/relative URLs or the pack assets are demonstrably unused for card rendering.
- The registry is total: an unknown pack ref, a missing bundled file, or an empty registry degrades to base content and never throws.
- Unit tests cover source ordering, additive registration and degradation, and pass in the `unit` project.
data.title: Pack-source registry and bundled source

# Browser boot discovers bundled packs

**Parent:** MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD (Make card packs available in the browser distribution)

## Summary

Make Main Street boot discover card packs from the bundled pack source when no Electron content directory or bridge is present, so the Card Packs panel lists the residential pack (gated) instead of "No card packs installed", with no `tce-packs://` request in the browser path.

## Goal (user story)

> As a player of the web build, I want the residential card pack to appear in the Card Packs panel, so the DLC works in the distributed browser version and not only under the Electron launcher.

## Minimal Implementation

- Change the boot gate (`bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks` in `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`) so an absent `window.tce.contentDir` falls back to the bundled source instead of bailing to base content.
- Update `shouldBootstrapPacks` in `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` so the browser path still triggers discovery before scene setup.
- Route browser content through the pack-source registry transports (from `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` child "Pack-source registry and bundled source") and resolve asset references to same-origin/relative URLs under `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`.
- Verify the listing renders the bundled residential pack as a locked row with a `[ Purchase ]` control (via the existing `CardPackListing` / `openCardPacksPanel` wiring in `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`).
- Keep the Electron content-directory path byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Deliverables

- Boot fallback and lifecycle gate changes
- Same-origin/relative asset and CSV resolution for the browser path
- Unit coverage for the boot fallback and the base-path (`BASE_URL`) behaviour

## Dependencies

- Depends on: "Pack-source registry and bundled source" (the registry it consumes).

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetCardPacks.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/CardPackListing.browser.test.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

- In the browser build (no `window.tce.contentDir` and no Electron bridges), Main Street boot discovers the bundled pack so the Card Packs panel lists the residential pack instead of "No card packs installed".
- The pack remains **gated** in the browser: while locked its cards stay out of play and its listing row offers a `[ Purchase ]` control.
- Pack CSV and asset URLs resolve in the browser with **no `tce-packs://` request**; either the bundled source supplies same-origin/relative URLs or the pack assets are demonstrably unused for card rendering.
- Any same-origin fallback respects the web base path (`import.meta.env.BASE_URL`, the GitHub Pages project base `/tce-main-street/`), not just `/`.
- The browser path degrades totally: a missing bundled pack leaves the panel on base content and never throws.
- Unit tests cover the boot fallback and the base-path resolution.
data.title: Browser boot discovers bundled packs

**discovered-from:MS-0MV53CFUS004DFX1**

**Symptom.** A concurrent push advanced `origin/dev` while `implement.py finish` was committing. The push failed non-fast-forward and the recovery branch in `phase_finish` crashed with `Unhandled exception: name 'cwd' is not defined` (the `git rebase origin/dev` call uses `cwd=cwd`, but `phase_finish` has no `cwd` local). The work item was reset to `open` and the commit was left unpushed (the worktree was already removed), requiring manual rebase/push recovery.

**Location.** `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py`, the `PushNonFastForwardError` handler inside `phase_finish`.

**Expected.** The recovery path rebases onto `origin/dev`, retries the push, and preserves state on failure — without an unhandled exception.

**Suggested fix.** Use the discovered `worktree_path` for the rebase `cwd` (or defer the rebase to a temp worktree); add a regression test.
data.title: implement.py non-fast-forward push recovery references undefined cwd
